title: Every asset in SparkLend's Gnosis deployment is Frozen, winding the chain down asset by asset
content:
The SparkLend Gnosis configuration (A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.2.2) lists nine assets, and every one records `Reserve State: Frozen` — GNO (.2.1), WETH (.2.2), USDT (.2.3), sDai (.2.4), wstETH (.2.5), USDC (.2.6), USDC.e (.2.7), WXDAI (.2.8), EURe (.2.9). By contrast the Ethereum deployment in the same chunk is overwhelmingly `Active`, with only rETH, tBTC and ezETH frozen.

Frozen means "all activities may occur except for supplying and borrowing." A whole deployment in that state is a deployment closed to new business and open only for exit.

What is notable is the *mechanism*: there is no chain-level or deployment-level shutdown in the Artifact's vocabulary. Retiring an entire network is done by setting the same per-asset switch nine times. The blast radius of the primitive is one market, so a full wind-down is expressible without adding a more powerful control that could also be triggered in error or by a compromised key.

The cost is that the intent lives nowhere. Nothing in the document says "Gnosis is being retired" — that conclusion is only available by reading nine sibling subdocuments and noticing they all say the same thing. A reader checking a single Gnosis asset sees a frozen market; only the aggregate reveals a deployment exit. This is the recurring trade in the Spark Artifact: uniform low-level records are precise and auditable, and systematically omit the decision that produced them.
description: All nine Gnosis markets — GNO, WETH, USDT, sDai, wstETH, USDC, USDC.e, WXDAI, EURe — carry Reserve State Frozen, with no chain-level shutdown switch invoked.
